newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels say government troops defecting.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels say government troops defecting.

text.p: Zairean rebels said government troops were joining their campaign to march on Kinshasa but reports from the northeastern town of Bunia said the army was well placed to defend the town from a rebel attack.

The military commander of the rebels, Andre Kissasse Ngandu, said in an interview published on Sunday that more than 300 Zairean army soldiers, including a colonel and three captains, had defected to try to overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko.
He dismissed predictions that the rebels, known as the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, would not have the strength to carry their campaign through.

The rebellion broke out near the Rwandan border in October among Zaireans of Rwandan origin and the rebels, backed by the Rwandan army, have routed the Zairean army across a front about 450 km (280 miles) long from north to south.
Rebels based in the northeastern town of Beni said on Sunday their forces were attacking Bunia, 150 km (90 miles) to the northeast, and would eventually capture it.
"Bunia hasn't fallen yet. We're still in the process of taking it," said a rebel officer who gave his name as Jacques.
But people in the northeastern capital Kisangani quoted residents of Bunia, contacted by radio, as saying the army had secured the town and the rebels had not entered.
They said Kisangani itself was quiet and insecurity from unruly Zairean soldiers was no longer a problem.
The rebels have said they are close to and even inside Kisangani but no independent sources have confirmed this.

Commander Ngandu, in the interview in the Kenyan newspaper the Sunday Standard, said: "As I speak now, over 300 of Mobutu's soldiers have already joined our forces... We have one colonel and three army captains who have laid down their weapons and joined our struggle. They are fed up with Mobutu. Then say we cannot reach Kinshasa. Is Kinshasa in heaven?"

"Everyone, mothers, children and men are joining us every night and day to fight our common enemy. Yet they dream that we cannot take Kinshasa. We have the arms and the people have the will to fight. We will reach Kinshasa very soon," he added.

The commander ridiculed attempts to find out the number of Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire by aerial reconnaissance and said the United Nations was playing with the number of refugees missing as an excuse to bring in foreign forces.

A mainly Canadian multinational force, with a mandate to help the refugees, has set up headquarters in the Ugandan capital Kampala but it cannot move yet because of objections from both the rebels and the Zairean government.

The Canadian commander of the force, Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril, headed for eastern Zaire on Sunday in an attempt to gather more information about the plight of the refugees. He may also meet rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
Officers at the force headquarters in Kampala said he should have crossed the border but they could not confirm that he did.
Kabila says the force is redundant because most of the refugees have gone home to Rwanda. Analysts say he also fears the multinational force might restore Mobutu's authority.
Commander Ngandu said the rebels particularly objected to French intervention in Zaire.

"France continues meddling in Zairean and African affairs. They love causing pain and suffering to African countries... We are ready for them. And if they come as soldiers, then we are ready to fight them as soldiers. But we will not allow them to roam about freely in our country," he said.
But in Paris the French minister in charge of African affairs said in comments released on Saturday that the international military force for Zaire was no longer viable.
"It's now out of the question (for the force to be deployed)," Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain told the weekly newspaper Le Journal du Dimanche.
Godfrain said the priority now was to organise a conference of countries from the Great Lakes region of Africa.
